title: AI-assisted construction takeoff for quantity surveyors
problem: Quantity surveyors and estimators still spend substantial time measuring drawings/PDFs and moving quantities into spreadsheets or estimating systems.
target_user: Small construction estimators, quantity surveyors and subcontractors with repetitive takeoff workflows
solution_wedge: Undetermined. A generic AI takeoff tool is already crowded; a narrower trade-specific or workflow-specific wedge would be required.
evidence_summary: Public discussions describe takeoff as repetitive manual work often performed in Bluebeam/PDF tools and Excel, but current evidence is not yet strong enough to establish a differentiated opportunity.
reason: Pain appears real, but competition is significant and no sufficiently sharp wedge has been identified yet.
next_step: Only promote if repeated signals reveal a specific trade, document type, handoff, or failure mode underserved by current takeoff tools.

title: Maintainable deterministic legal document assembly for small firms
problem: Law firms with complex conditional documents still maintain fragile Word/VBA/HotDocs-style logic; every clause change risks breaking templates, and institutional knowledge is often trapped with one technical lawyer or consultant.
target_user: Small and mid-size transactional, banking, estate, family, and niche legal practices with high-volume rule-based document sets
solution_wedge: Make existing deterministic templates maintainable: visual clause dependency graph, tests/regression checks, versioning, and safe editing by non-programmers rather than another AI drafting tool.
evidence_summary: Fresh 2026 legal-tech discussions describe broken mailmerge/conditional-clause workflows, high maintenance burden, coder dependency, and strong value from deterministic automation. However Gavel, HotDocs, Knackly, Woodpecker, PatternBuilder, Contract Express and others already cover much of document assembly.
reason: Repeated pain is credible and the maintenance/testing angle is sharper than generic document automation, but direct tools are mature and willingness to pay specifically for template-maintenance infrastructure is unproven.
next_step: Promote only if 5+ firms independently report template maintenance/regression as the bottleneck and existing products do not solve safe change management.
